metadata.case_name: CHUI WAI KAM MICHELLE v. GILLESPIE JOHN THOMAS

injuries.description: soft tissue injury of her neck as a result of the Accident
source: The experts agreed that the plaintiff suffered from soft tissue injury of her neck as a result of the Accident.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon at neck level

injuries.description: retrolisthesis at the C5/6 level of her cervical spine
source: The doctors suspected that the retrolisthesis[1] at the C5/6 level of her cervical spine was caused by trauma.
injuries.icd_description: Dislocation of other specified cervical vertebra

injuries.description: Anterior marginal osteophytes at the C5 and C6 vertebrae with desiccation and narrowing of the C5/6 intervertebral disc consistent with spondylosis; mild to moderate degree of broad-based posterior C5/6 disc protrusion indenting the theca and anterior cervical cord causing left foraminal stenosis with impingement on the left C6 exiting nerve root
source: Anterior marginal osteophytes at the C5 and C6 vertebrae were seen, with desiccation and narrowing of the C5/6 intervertebral disc, consistent with spondylosis. There was mild to moderate degree of broad-based posterior C5/6 disc protrusion, indenting the theca and anterior cervical cord. The protruded disc was also causing left foraminal stenosis with impingement on the left C6 exiting nerve root. There was mild right foraminal stenosis due to osteophytic encroachment by unco-vertebral joint marginal spur, but there was no significant impingement on the right C6 exiting nerve root.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of nerve root of cervical spine

manifestations.description: Burning sensation radiating down her left upper limb
Active neck flexion and extension reduced to about 1/2 of the normal range; neck rotation reduced to about 1/3 of the normal range (on initial physiotherapy assessment)
Muscle power over her right upper limb slightly decreased (on initial physiotherapy assessment)
Pain and numbness in her upper limbs
Pain and numbness in her back and right leg
Residual impairment in her neck, such as weakness, pain and numbness (after maximal medical improvement)

source: She was given a soft neck collar on 21 September 2011.

treatments_received.treatment: admitted to the orthopaedics ward at Yan Chai Hospital (24 September 2011 to 28 September 2011)
source: The plaintiff was called back to YCH on 24 September 2011, and was admitted to the orthopaedics ward. The doctors suspected that the retrolisthesis[1] at the C5/6 level of her cervical spine was caused by trauma. Her condition remained stable, and she was discharged on 28 September 2011.

The plaintiff started physiotherapy on 14 October 2011. The attending physiotherapist recorded her complaint as pain over her left neck region with burning sensation radiating down her left upper limb. There was also tenderness over her right neck. The active neck flexion and extension was noted to be 1/2 the normal range, and neck rotation was 1/3 the normal range. Muscle power over her right upper limb was noted to be slightly decreased. After 12 sessions of physiotherapy, the plaintiff reported 80% subjective improvement.

treatments_received.treatment: occupational therapy (7 sessions at YCH between 7 October 2011 and 15 December 2011)
source: The plaintiff also received 7 sessions of occupational therapy at YCH between 7 October 2011 and 15 December 2011.

treatments_received.treatment: chiropractic treatment by Dr Simon Lee at California Pain Care Centre (from 23 April 2014 to last treatment on 16 June 2014)
source: The plaintiff sought treatment from Dr Simon Lee, a chiropractor practising at California Pain Care Centre in Mongkok, starting from 23 April 2014.
Up to the last treatment on 16 June 2014, the plaintiff was said to have 50% recovery.
She thus visited a Chinese bonesetter seeking to alleviate her neck pain. She claimed that there was some relief to her pain and discomfort after 3-4 visits.

treatments_received.treatment: bonesetter treatment on 9 September 2014 (different bonesetter) and subsequent private practitioner consultation for skin sensitivity
source: The plaintiff then claimed that on 9 September 2014, her right hand suddenly became so weak that she could not even hold the handrail properly when she went down stairs. She sprained her right hand as a result. Hence, she visited a bonesetter (different from the first one she visited) for treatment. ... But on the next day, her skin became sensitive to the Chinese medicine applied by the bonesetter. Thus, she consulted a private practitioner for treatment. There were receipts evidencing both treatments.

An MRI was done on 11 April 2015. Anterior marginal osteophytes at the C5 and C6 vertebrae were seen, with desiccation and narrowing of the C5/6 intervertebral disc, consistent with spondylosis. There was mild to moderate degree of broad-based posterior C5/6 disc protrusion, indenting the theca and anterior cervical cord. The protruded disc was also causing left foraminal stenosis with impingement on the left C6 exiting nerve root. There was mild right foraminal stenosis due to osteophytic encroachment by unco-vertebral joint marginal spur, but there was no significant impingement on the right C6 exiting nerve root.

treatments_future.treatment: symptomatic treatment from time to time (private sector)
source: She would continue to suffer from some residual impairment in her neck, such as weakness, pain and numbness. She would need symptomatic treatment from time to time.

losses.description: Residual impairment in her neck, such as weakness, pain and numbness
